Thanks Marissa — and thanks Dylan for running these. A couple of quick follow-ups from our side: 

- Can you confirm the p99 numbers at ~8k tokens with KV cache enabled vs disabled? Our production workload sometimes disables KV cache for privacy reasons; p99 sensitivity there is a blocker.
- What GPU was used for the runs and what batch sizes correspond to the throughput numbers in the CSV? We're trying to compare against our internal perf matrix (A100 vs H100).
- Is there any guidance on warm vs cold starts? We saw significantly higher tail latency on cold start in our tests.

If it's easier, happy to jump on a 20-min call with Dylan — but a short reply with those numbers would be great so I can share with engineering.

On Sat, Feb 21, 2026 at 10:15 AM Jared Young <jared.young@bump.com> wrote:
> Can you confirm the p99 numbers at ~8k tokens with KV cache enabled vs disabled?
> What GPU was used and what batch sizes correspond to the throughput numbers?
> Any guidance on warm vs cold starts?

Hi Jared — thanks for the questions, good ones. Short answers (details attached):

- KV cache: With KV cache enabled we measured p99 ~ 2100 ms at 8k tokens (model: redwood-open-1, quantized FP16, H100), with cache disabled p99 increases to ~4200 ms in the same setup. This matches the expected O(n) behavior when cache is rebuilt each request.
- GPU & batch sizes: Tests were run on an H100 nvlink-connected instance (4x H100 for scale tests). Throughput numbers in latency-results-8k.csv show per-GPU throughput at batch sizes 1, 2, 4, 8 (columns included). For reference: batch 4 on H100 ~ 18 seq/s per GPU at 8k tokens; batch 8 ~ 30 seq/s (higher variability).
- Warm vs cold: Cold start (first request after container spin-up) added ~800–1200 ms tail due to model load and kernel JIT. For steady-state producers we recommend keeping warm pools or using pre-warmed standby to avoid that hit.

I've attached the summary PDF and the raw CSV with the per-run metrics. Full dataset and run configs are in the linked Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-benchmarks 

If you'd like, we can replicate the run on A100 to give you a direct comparison — happy to set that up if you can share preferred instance type.

Attachments: redwood-latency-benchmarks-20260220.pdf, latency-results-8k.csv

Regards,
